input: Assess the credit and counterparty risk of AMC Entertainment

output.risk_rationale: As of 2026-11-04, credit and counterparty risk is elevated: Fitch's B-/Positive rating and history of substantial negative free cash flow indicate meaningful speculative-grade risk (https://www.fitchratings.com/research/corporate-finance/fitch-rates-amc-entertainment-new-first-lien-debt-b-rr3-21-09-2026). AMC reported $3.9142 billion of corporate borrowing principal at June 30 and warned that historical cash-burn rates were unsustainable, although first-half operating cash flow improved to positive $106.9 million (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1411579/000141157926000059/amc-20260630x10q.htm). Preliminary August 31 cash of $832.5 million and the completed October 5 refinancing extending major maturities to 2031 and 2033 mitigate near-term risk, but that cash balance predates the refinancing and post-closing liquidity was not verified (https://investor.amctheatres.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001104659-26-109129/tm2625696d2_ex99-1.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1411579/000110465926113853/tm2627016d1_8k.htm).

ownership.value: Public company with publicly held common stock. The latest proxy identifies institutional beneficial holders including Pentwater Capital Management LP and Discovery Capital Management LLC; a recent change of control or controlling sponsor was not verified.

distress_signals.summary: The Q2 Form 10-Q warned that historical cash-burn rates were not sustainable long-term and that additional liquidity beyond twelve months was not assured. Management nevertheless believed existing cash plus operating cash generation would cover operations and obligations for the next twelve months; this is a management liquidity warning, not an identified auditor substantial-doubt opinion.

FY2025 non-cash long-lived-asset impairments totaled $43.5 million, affecting 47 U.S. theatres and 20 international theatres. These impairments indicate asset underperformance but do not establish that those theatres closed.

financials: quantified undrawn revolving-credit availability was not verified.

credit_ratings.summary: Latest verified S&P issuer credit rating: B-/Stable, upgraded from CCC+/Negative on improved operating performance and expected credit-metric improvement.

Fitch affirmed the long-term issuer default rating at B- with a Positive outlook. New first-lien debt was rated B/RR3 and second-lien debt CCC/RR6. Fitch's issuer history also records a new B- rating on September 8, 2026.

Investing.com reported Moody's upgrade of AMC's corporate family rating to B3 from Caa2, with the outlook changed to Positive from Stable. The speculative-grade liquidity rating improved to SGL-3 from SGL-4. This rating action was verified through secondary reporting rather than an opened Moody's release.

debt_events.summary: AMC entered a lender letter agreement providing for indenture amendments to facilitate refinancing of existing AMC and Odeon debt. Implementation was targeted by February 23, 2026, and AMC committed to a consent fee payable in common stock. The filing did not describe this as a default or covenant-breach cure.

AMC stated that it believed it was in full compliance with outstanding-debt agreements and related covenants. The Form 10-Q reported no defaults upon senior securities; this is a June 30 status, not confirmation of all obligations through November 4.

Completed $3.97 billion of refinancing: $2.0 billion of 8.875% first-lien notes due 2031, an $850 million first-lien term loan due October 5, 2031, and a $1.12 billion second-lien term loan at 11.25% due October 5, 2033. Existing AMC and Odeon term loans were repaid, the tender offer settled, and all $903.4 million of Muvico 1.5L notes were redeemed. The financing extends major maturities but does not establish that total debt fell by the amount refinanced.
